content: 1. The absorption of tetracyclines may be impaired by certain products, potentially reducing their efficacy. It is recommended to separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products and monitor the patient closely. 2. Magnesium supplements can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 3. Multivalent cation-containing products, such as magnesium, can form insoluble complexes with tetracyclines, reducing their absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. To avoid this, administer magnesium at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after tetracycline. Monitor the patient closely. 4. Manganese can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 5. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and coadministration with antibacterial agents may reduce their efficacy. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Monitor the patient closely. 6. Molybdenum can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 7. Multivitamins containing multivalent cations may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. Monitor the patient closely. 8. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of nafcillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 9. Omadacycline may increase the effects of pancuronium due to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of penicillin G aqueous due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 11. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of penicillin G benzathine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 12. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of penicillin G procaine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 13. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of penicillin VK due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 14. Omadacycline may decrease the effects of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 15. Polysaccharide iron can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 16. Pyridoxine can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 17. Sodium acid phosphate can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 18. Sodium bicarbonate can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 19. Sodium citrate/citric acid can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 20. Sodium phosphate rectal can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 21. Sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 22. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride can decrease the levels of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 23. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate can decrease the levels of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 24. Omadacycline may increase the effects of succinylcholine due to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Thiamine can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 26. Tretinoin may increase the toxicity of omadacycline through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of oral retinoids with tetracyclines may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri/intracranial hypertension. 27. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 28. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 29. Omadacycline may increase the effects of vecuronium due to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Vitamin B2 can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 31. Omadacycline may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 32. Zinc can decrease the levels or effects of omadacycline by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. 33. Hypersensitivity to any tetracycline has been reported. Life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been observed with other tetracyclines. 34. Omadacycline may cause discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy. Pregnant women should discontinue omadacycline as soon as pregnancy is recognized. 35. Tetracyclines are excreted in human milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions on bone and tooth development in nursing infants, omadacycline is not recommended for breastfeeding women. Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose. 36. Use of omadacycline in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to provide benefit to the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 37. As with other antibiotics, the use of omadacycline may result in the overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, including fungi. 38. In clinical trials for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP), a mortality imbalance was observed, with 8 deaths (2%) in patients treated with omadacycline compared to 4 deaths (1%) in patients treated with moxifloxacin. Causes of death varied and included worsening or complications of infection and underlying conditions. All deaths occurred in patients aged >65 years, most of whom had multiple comorbidities. Monitor clinical response to therapy closely, particularly in patients at higher risk for mortality.
